newsitem.title: CANADA: Saskatchewan harvests 53 pct of crops vs 73 pct.
newsitem.headline: Saskatchewan harvests 53 pct of crops vs 73 pct.

text.p: Saskatchewan harvested 53 percent of all crops through the week ended September 30, compared to the five-year average of 73 percent, Saskatchewan Agriculture said.

Killing frosts were reported in many areas but damage estimates were not available. With 50 percent of spring wheat harvested, 78 percent was expected to grade number one, 16 percent number two, and five percent number three. The estimate should fall once harvest resumes.
The 10-year average for spring wheat has 47 percent at No1, 24 percent at No2, 19 percent at No3 and 10 percent feed.
Rain halted harvest progress which advanced to 53 percent coplete from 52 percent the past week.
Southern Saskatchewan saw an average nine mm of rain. Frost damage was reported in all areas. Rain caused sprouting and quality loss on swathed and standing crops.
Central Saskatchewan saw an average eight mm of rain. Frost damage was reported in all areas. Rain caused sprouting in the west central region.
Northern Saskatchewan saw an average 10 mm of rain. Rain caused bleaching, sprouting and lodging in standing crops.
